\subsubsection{Not Yet Verified}\label{sss:pixtop-open}

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
  \item \textbf{Stability.} No ac or loop-gain run exists on the assembled
    channel; one is being set up and is not yet reported. The phase margins of
    Section~\ref{sss:pixel-grid} were measured with an ideal \(R_f\) and an
    ideal reference, and the programmable ladder has never been simulated
    inside the loop.
  \item \textbf{Noise, power, corners.} None. Every number here is one process
    point at one temperature, and no test carries a supply-current output.
  \item \textbf{Monte Carlo.} Blocked twice over: the model section this setup
    names carries no statistics, and A2's two compensation capacitors still
    have their mismatch flag clear. Either alone produces a run that completes
    and yields a tidy, wrong distribution.
  \item \textbf{The converter at schematic level.} Its capacitor array exists
    only in the extracted view (Section~\ref{sss:pixtop-adc}), so the code the
    schematic tests report is stuck and is deliberately left unspecced.
  \item \textbf{Wiring.} Three items are drawn but not connected. The sixteen
    test-port multiplexer inputs are undriven, so the debug path selects
    between floating nodes on demand. The two DAC supply blocks' outputs reach
    nothing, which is why the supply-modulation defect of
    Section~\ref{sss:dacr2r12-supply} is not exercised in this cell. And there
    is no buffer between the common-mode rail and the converter multiplexer:
    selecting that slot loads the bare ladder output --- which is also A2's
    reference --- pulling the common mode to \SI{0.731}{\volt} and throwing the
    transimpedance output from \SI{1.25}{\volt} to \SI{16}{\milli\volt} for
    more than \SI{4}{\micro\second}, at every conversion. It collapses the one
    measurement the gain-independent zero of Section~\ref{sss:pixtop-zero}
    depends on. The output slot is quiet by comparison:
    \SI{0.74}{\milli\volt} on the common mode and \SI{3.5}{\milli\volt} on the
    output over a whole \SI{21}{\micro\second} run.
\end{itemize}
